title: The Stolen Blessing
reflectionText: The voice was Jacob's voice, but the hands were the hands of Esau — and the blessing, once spoken, could not be called back. Then came the cry, great and bitter: Bless me — me also, my father. What is it to stand where Esau stood, asking whether there is only one blessing?
editorialNotes: Text-First Story Factory 2.0 Batch A (journey backlog G9, approved 2026-07-22). Genesis 27, absent both lanes (verified 0 anchor hits); right-adjacent neighbor 1018 (Genesis 28:10-22, Jacob's Ladder) picks up after the flight. Boundary: chapter 27 only — no birthright backstory from Genesis 25, no Bethel material from Genesis 28, and the 25:23 oracle is NOT imported as Rebekah's motive; her motive is left unstated as in the source. SHORT + FULL + LONG (WEB 457w / 863w / 1100w; KJV 498w / 899w / 980w): the 46-verse dialogue-dense chapter (~1161 WEB source words) honestly supports all three bands. LONG renders the charge, the scheme, the three verification probes, both blessings, and both Rebekah speeches; FULL compresses Isaac's reply (v37) and the anti-blessing (vv39-40) to reported speech; SHORT compresses the scheme and omits v46 (the daughters-of-Heth complaint) — documented compression. All emotion is source-stated (Isaac trembled violently; Esau's exceedingly great and bitter cry and weeping; Esau's hatred; Rebekah weary of her life). No invented interiority for Jacob. CODEX-AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-07-23 (Finding 1, accepted as genuine ADR-031 L2 failure): the KJV LONG was fully re-authored from a lightly-paraphrased near-transcription (was run 33 / 84.8% coverage) into an independently-composed retelling that converts most of the chapter's dialogue to reported speech in KJV register and reorganizes narrative emphasis (now run 10 / 40.8% coverage, 980w). Essential turning-point dialogue kept direct (the voice-vs-hands line; Esau's 'Bless me, even me also, O my father'; 'Hast thou but one blessing'). WEB SHORT/FULL/LONG and KJV SHORT/FULL unchanged.
